- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable, 4.8.beta4, likely earlier versions as well

When the `Accessibility Support` setting is set to `Always Active`, you can no longer resize the various interface panels of the Editor, like making the bottom panel bigger/smaller.

This seems to mostly be specific to the `3D` view, as resizing still works in the `2D/Script Editor` views. (Though that seems to feel more jittery as well, IMO.)

Having the `Always Active` setting on is important for some niche, unsupported-by-default accessibility programs, such as certain BetterTouchTool behaviours on MacOS.

I am unsure if this is MacOS-specific, as I don't have a Windows/Linux machine.

LightmapGI bake hangs with endless "Inconsistency found in triangulation while building BSP"

Godot: master (b070e63b16), macOS arm64, Forward+

Godot v4.8.beta (dc36fd23f) - macOS Golden Gate (27.2.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor (3024x1964 @ 120.00 Hz) - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M4 Pro (12 threads) - 24.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

Bake on the attached scene never ends. Console is spammed with:

```
    WARNING: Inconsistency found in triangulation while building BSP, probe interpolation quality may degrade a bit.
         at: _compute_bsp_tree (scene/3d/lightmap_gi.cpp:677)
```

Pressing Ctrl+C in the terminal does not stop the process. You can stop it only with the `kill` command.

[image]

[image]

Scene is just a BoxMesh 30x3x30 (add_uv2) and LightmapGI. I also tried other subdiv options.
Other heights break too: for `30 x h x 30`, where `h` is 1.0 .. 7.3 with step 0.1. 59 of 64 examples give a broken triangulation.
Some of them finish, but with thousands of warnings.

This was discovered not in a synthetic scene, but in a very real one. However, I cannot provide it, as it depends on far too many resources:
[image]

What I found:

- `Delaunay3D::tetrahedralize` returns overlapping tetrahedra for these probes (50 points on a 5x2x5 grid). For 30x3x30 it gives 192 tets, total volume is 3.99x the box. Same points in exact arithmetic: 96 tets, 1.00x.
- Grid points are cospherical. `circum_sphere_compute()` divides in R128, and for simplices touching the root simplex the error is bigger than the 1e-10 in `simplex_contains()`. So a point on the sphere sometimes counts as inside, the cavity gets wrong and zero volume simplices appear. For them `determinant` is 0, `center` is ~2e17 and `circum_r2` is 0, so they are never removed again.
- Then `_compute_bsp_tree()` can't split the overlapping tets and goes to the fallback. The fallback also looks broken: `centers` is filled only for `i == 0`, and `indices_under.push_back(min_d_idx)` pushes 0 instead of `p_simplex_indices[0]`. It peels one tet per level, so the tree explodes.

I checked this with a copy of `tetrahedralize()` built with `thirdparty/misc/r128.h`, it gives exactly the same tets as Godot saves into `.lmbake`.

I have a solution to this problem, which we made together with Claude.

A detailed description can be found in [technical_notes.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35302430/technical_notes.md).
The solution implements exact predicates for already-quantized integers, using a double-filter approach combined with 256-bit arithmetic (see sections 4–6).
There is a rigorous mathematical guarantee that the fallback code path will never be triggered.
This is confirmed by tests: 11 out of 34 checks fail with the original code, whereas 0 fail with the new implementation (see section 8).
Execution speed remains unaffected (see the table in section 9).
You can view a comparison with the current version here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...nklbdev:godot:nklbdev/lightmap-probe-triangulation

Should I submit a pull request containing the contents of this branch, or would you prefer to conduct your own in-depth investigation and implement a fix independently?

ZIPReader heap over-read (up to ~64KB) when iterating a corrupted zip

- Reproducible in: 4.4.stable, master (67421f36e5)

Linux x86_64

`ZIPReader.get_files()` can read up to ~64KB past a heap buffer when processing a crafted zip. the over-read bytes end up in the returned filename strings, so script code sees heap memory.

how it happens: in `godot_unzip_get_current_file_info` (core/io/zip_io.cpp), the first `unzGetCurrentFileInfo64` call can fail on a corrupted entry. when it fails, the `unz_file_info64` struct on the stack keeps its stale value from the previous iteration (previous entry's `size_filename`). the code then sizes the retry `LocalVector<char>` buffer to that stale (small) value. the second call succeeds and overwrites `size_filename` with the real (attacker-controlled, up to 65535) value. then `String::utf8(buffer.ptr(), r_file_info.size_filename)` reads the full large length from the undersized buffer.

confirmed under ASan with a replica built against the real vendored minizip: `READ of size 60000 ... 0 bytes after 8-byte region`.

the over-read data feeds into the `PackedStringArray` returned to GDScript, so it leaks heap content where UTF-8 valid. large lengths crash on unmapped pages.

any game opening user-provided zip files (mod packs, asset downloads) can trigger this.

[mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35228898/mrp.zip)

1. open the MRP project
2. run it
3. with ASan: heap-buffer-overflow READ. without ASan: filename strings contain leaked heap bytes or the engine crashes.

Deadlock when a WorkerThreadPool pump task runs a task that needs the main thread

- Reproducible in 4.7.stable (5b4e0cb0f), official mono build
- Reproducible in master (67421f36e5 as of 20/11/2026)
- I didn't test any older versions sorry

Steam Deck OLED, Ryzen 9 5900X + RTX 4080 (Fedora 45)

I might be doing something dumb but, in transitioning from one scene to another,using ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request(). The load task ran on the physics pump thread. During the load an ArrayMesh was duplicated (from a Terrain3D mesh asset), which reads surfaces back through RenderingServer::mesh_get_surface() and waited for the main thread. The main thread was in PhysicsServer3DWrapMT::sync(). Whole game froze on the loading screen, all threads asleep.

From what I could find this is the chain that leads to the lock.
- With physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread=true, PhysicsServer3DWrapMT runs _thread_loop() as a WorkerThreadPool pump task. Between command flushes it calls WorkerThreadPool::yield().
- While yielding, WorkerThreadPool::_wait_collaboratively() takes the next queued task and runs it on the pump thread. Only other pump tasks are skipped (worker_thread_pool.cpp, the task_to_process->is_pump_task check).
- Every frame the main thread calls PhysicsServer3DWrapMT::sync(), which does push_and_sync() and waits for the pump to flush.
- If the task the pump picked up waits for the main thread, nothing can move: the main thread waits for the pump, the pump is inside a task waiting for the main thread.

1. Open the MRP (or run headless: godot --headless --path mrp).
2. Watch the output. It prints a frame counter, then within a few frames prints DEADLOCK: no frame for 5 s (a watchdog thread prints this and kills the process).
3. Set physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread=false and it should pass with no deadlocks

4.0 .stable.official.92bee43ad (same issue)
Also appeared in tracy enabled builds of the above, which was used to find the offending section

Godot v4.7.2.stable (ed1daf0bf) - Bazzite 45.20261112 (Kinoite) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti (nvidia; 620.70.06) - AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 30.49 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

Setting the joint property of a PhysicalBone3D off the main thread (eg in a worker) waits for the physics server even when the joint is not in the tree. since physics runs on the main thread and it uses push_and_ret, it blocks for a frame per property, per joint

1. Set physics on the main thread - this is the default setting
2. In code, build a packed scene with multiple PhysicalBone3D nodes, make sure they have non-default joint properties
3. Call instantiate() on the packed scene from the main thread - this is fast
4. Call instantiate() from a WorkerThreadPool task - this is magnitudes slower

The repro uses 20 cone bodies each with 2 joint properties changed - on official 4.7.2
| called from | time |
|---|---|
| main thread | ~0.2ms |
| worker thread | ~1,550ms / ~223 frames |

5. Set `physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread=true`
6. Observe no issue

Tested on 4.0 and the issue appears there too, didn't seem worth tracking further back as 3 to 4 changes were major

1. JointData::_set starts with
```
bool is_valid_cone = j.is_valid() && PhysicsServer3D::get_singleton()->joint_get_type(j) == PhysicsServer3D::JOINT_TYPE_CONE_TWIST;
```
2. `joint_get_type` is `FUNC1RC` in `PhysicsServer3DWrapMT` and from a non physics server thread, that's `push_and_ret` (blocking till return)
3. PhysicsServer has to flush it's command queue
4. PhysicsServer in the main thread only does this when the next physics call is made or it steps?
5. `joint_get_type` can thus take up to a frame to return
6. Since push and ret is blocking, that's up to a frame, per property, per joint

Using `physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread = true` solves this, because the PhysicsServer drains its queue continuously

[Repro Skeleton 3d.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35218249/Repro.Skeleton.3d.zip)

Run the default scene, with and without `physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread`

If you extend a script that references a virtual method it doesn't implement, in the release exported build the extended script will throw a misleading error `SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: Could not resolve class {class name}`. "Misleading" because it implies that for some reason your class is just missing, even though the real issue is it has an error.

Because this doesn't happen in the editor and debug builds, and real error is not reported correctly in release exported builds either, it makes it surprisingly difficult to debug.

---

If you have a base class like this
```
class_name ShortcutButton
extends Button

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
		_pressed()
```

and extend it with a class like this
```
extends ShortcutButton

func _pressed() -> void:
	print("Thing")
```

It will work perfectly in the editor, but in the exported build will throw an error `SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: Could not resolve class "ShortcutButton".` and will fail to load the script. No other errors will be printed.

[image]

If you however try to load the script directly, e.g. like this
```
func _ready() -> void:
	load("res://shortcut_button.gd")
```
it will correctly print the error that causes `ShortcutButton` to not be resolved: `SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: Function "_pressed()" not found in base self.`. This also only occurs in the release exported build.

1. Add a script that references a virtual method, e.g. script that extends `Button` and references `_pressed()`
2. Add another script that extends the previous one and attach it to a node
3. Export release build of the project and run it
In the console you will see `SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: Could not resolve class {class name}`

TwoBoneIK3D and SpringBoneSimulator3D leak memory when freed

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable.official
- The current `master` source (commit 73ca6be2ce) appears to have the same code path (see below); not run.

Windows 11 (10.0.26200), headless (`--headless`), AMD Ryzen 5 7600X3D

Freeing a `TwoBoneIK3D` or a `SpringBoneSimulator3D` after it has processed with a valid bone chain does not release all of its memory. The object count returns to where it was, but static memory grows by about 184 bytes per freed `TwoBoneIK3D` and about 300 bytes per freed `SpringBoneSimulator3D`. A game that builds and frees animated skeletons as characters come and go grows without bound. In our case it was about 0.1 MB a minute of static memory over an hour of play.

Output of the script below (1,000 skeletons built, processed for two frames, and freed per batch):

```
Godot 4.7.2-stable (official)
skeleton_only  static memory after each batch of 1000 (KiB): 24862 24862 24862 24862 24862 24862  | growth over the last 5 batches: 0 KiB, objects now 1483
two_bone_ik    static memory after each batch of 1000 (KiB): 25043 25223 25402 25582 25762 25941  | growth over the last 5 batches: 899 KiB, objects now 1483
spring_bone    static memory after each batch of 1000 (KiB): 26302 26599 26896 27193 27490 27787  | growth over the last 5 batches: 1484 KiB, objects now 1483
```

What appears to happen, from reading the source:

- **`TwoBoneIK3D`:** `~TwoBoneIK3D()` calls `clear_settings()`, which deletes each `TwoBoneIK3DSetting`. The setting holds `root_joint_solver_info` and `mid_joint_solver_info` as raw pointers (`two_bone_ik_3d.h`), allocated during processing. They are freed only by `TwoBoneIK3D::_clear_joints()` (`two_bone_ik_3d.cpp`), which deleting the setting never reaches.
- **`SpringBoneSimulator3D`:** `~SpringBoneSimulator3D()` calls `clear_settings()` → `set_setting_count(0)`, which `memdelete`s each `SpringBone3DSetting`. The setting's `LocalVector<SpringBone3DJointSetting *> joints` holds raw pointers, each with a raw `SpringBone3DVerletInfo *verlet`, and neither struct has a destructor.
  - The joints are freed only when the joint count is set again. Emptying each chain's root and end bone names before freeing the node does avoid the leak, which supports this reading.
- Setting `setting_count = 0` or calling `clear_settings()` before freeing does not help for `TwoBoneIK3D`.

A destructor on the setting structs that frees the solver/joint data, or calling `_clear_joints()` / the joint cleanup for each setting from `clear_settings()`, would likely fix both. Other `IKModifier3D` subclasses may be worth checking for the same pattern.

1. Create an empty project with the script below as `leak_repro.gd`.
2. Run `godot --headless --path <project> --script res://leak_repro.gd`.
3. Compare the static memory readings per mode: `skeleton_only` stays flat, `two_bone_ik` and `spring_bone` grow with every batch while the object count stays the same.

ZIPPacker does not actually use "store" method

v4.8.beta3.official [c51ff06e8]

Godot v4.8.beta3 - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue, 17 Nov 2026 22:28:33 +0000 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor (3440x1440 @ 75.05 Hz) - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7600 (RADV NAVI33) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700K (24 threads) - 31.10 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

The `ZIPPacker` docs say:

> `COMPRESSION_NONE = 0`
> Start a file with no compression. This is also known as the "Store" compression mode and is the fastest method of packing files inside a ZIP archive. Consider using this mode for files that are already compressed (such as JPEG, PNG, MP3, or Ogg Vorbis files).

However, internally, it still uses zlib a.k.a. deflate, just with `Z_NO_COMPRESSION` passed to it:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/73ca6be2cebd5192d8b279979d04f29ea45c266e/modules/zip/zip_packer.cpp#L113

To _actually_ use the "store" mode, we'd want to pass 0 instead of `Z_DEFLATED`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/73ca6be2cebd5192d8b279979d04f29ea45c266e/thirdparty/minizip/zip.h#L185

```
	var zip := ZIPPacker.new()
	zip.open("repro.zip")
	zip.compression_level = ZIPPacker.COMPRESSION_NONE
	zip.start_file("hello")
	zip.write_file("worldworldworldworldworldworldworldworldworldworldworld".to_utf8_buffer())
	zip.close_file()
	zip.close()
```

Then inspect the file with `unzip`:

```
$ unzip -l -v repro.zip 
Archive:  repro.zip

Editor freezes when a non-main thread loads a not-yet-imported glTF during the first filesystem scan

- Reproducible in: v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb]
- Not tested on other versions. The importer's `make_scene_preview` call was added in #96544 (4.4), so 4.4 and later are likely affected.

Godot v4.7.1.stable - Windows 10 - Vulkan(Forward+) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650

While the editor runs its first filesystem scan on startup, it imports any resource that is loaded and not yet imported, on the thread that requested the load. When that resource is a 3D scene (glTF/GLB/FBX), the scene importer calls `EditorInterface::make_scene_preview()`. That function only works on the main thread: it adds a node to `EditorNode`, calls `DisplayServer::process_events()` and runs `Main::iteration()` twice. Called from a worker thread, it prints the errors below and the editor stops responding. Windows reports the window as "Not Responding", and it never recovers until the process is killed.

Output
```
[repro] plugin entered, first scan running: true
[repro] thread loading res://models/zz_target.glb
ERROR: Adding children to a node inside the SceneTree is only allowed from the main thread. Use call_deferred("add_child",node).
   at: add_child (scene/main/node.cpp:1712)
   GDScript backtrace (most recent call first):
       [0] _load_on_thread (res://addons/repro/plugin.gd:15)
ERROR: Condition "!Thread::is_main_thread()" is true.
   at: process_events (platform/windows/display_server_windows.cpp:4225)
   GDScript backtrace (most recent call first):
       [0] _load_on_thread (res://addons/repro/plugin.gd:15)
[... 10 more lines]
```

The `print()` after the `load()` never runs, and the editor window stays frozen.

**Code path (4.7.1-stable):**

1. `EditorFileSystem` installs `ResourceImporter::load_on_startup` ([editor_file_system.cpp#L3821](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.1-stable/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp#L3821)). It is only cleared when the first scan's import pass finishes.
2. `ResourceFormatImporter::load()` routes through that hook ([resource_importer.cpp#L165](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.1-stable/core/io/resource_importer.cpp#L165)).
3. `_load_resource_on_startup()` calls `_reimport_file()` on the calling thread when the imported file is missing ([editor_file_system.cpp#L3468-L3486](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.1-stable/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp#L3468-L3486)).
4. `ResourceImporterScene::import()` calls `make_scene_preview()` ([resource_importer_scene.cpp#L3482](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.1-stable/editor/import/3d/resource_importer_scene.cpp#L3482)).
5. `make_scene_preview()` does the following from the worker thread:
   - `EditorNode::add_child()` ([editor_interface.cpp#L260](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.1-stable/editor/editor_interface.cpp#L260)), which raises the first error;
   - `DisplayServer::process_events()` ([#L316](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.1-stable/editor/editor_interface.cpp#L316)), which raises the second error;
   - `Main::iteration()` twice ([#L317-L318](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.1-stable/editor/editor_interface.cpp#L317-L318)), which hangs the editor.

`EditorProgress` already falls back to a background task when it is not on the main thread ([editor_node.cpp#L221-L245](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.1-stable/editor/editor_node.cpp#L221-L245)). Nothing guards the preview path.

**Control:** the same project with the same `load()` called directly in `_enter_tree()` (main thread, also during the first scan) imports the model and the editor stays responsive.

**Conditions:** the model's `.import` file exists but its output in `.godot/imported/` does not. This is the normal state after cloning a repository that commits `.import` files, after switching branches, or after deleting `.godot`. With no `.import` file at all, the threaded `load()` fails cleanly and nothing freezes.

**Real-world trigger:** the gdUnit4 editor plugin runs test discovery on a `Thread` at editor startup and `load()`s every test script along with its preloads. A project whose tests preload scenes that use unimported models hangs on open. It usually works after a restart, because it is a race between the editor's own import pass and the thread. With several unimported models it can fail on every open, because the editor freezes before its own import pass reaches them.

**Related:**

- #93159: the same class of bug in `ProgressDialog`, fixed in 4.3 by the `EditorProgress` thread check.
- #123127: `Main::iteration()` reached from inside an import.
- #112060 (open): reworks scene thumbnails, but `make_scene_preview()` still calls `add_child`, `process_events()` and `Main::iteration()`, and the importer still calls it without a thread check, so it does not fix this.

1. Unzip the attached MRP. It contains `models/zz_target.glb` with its `.import` file, an enabled editor plugin `addons/repro`, and no `.godot` folder.
2. Open the project in the editor.
3. The plugin's `_enter_tree()` starts a `Thread` that calls `load("res://models/zz_target.glb")` while the first scan is running.
4. The errors above are printed and the editor stops responding.

If it does not reproduce on a later open, delete the project's `.godot` folder and open it again.

	_thread = Thread.new()
	_thread.start(_load_on_thread)

AudioServer.get_input_frames() can crash on Android due to threading conflict on input_buffer

Reproducible in v4.8 beta 3

Android 13 (API 33) – OnePlus 8 IN2013 – arm64-v8a – Qualcomm – OxygenOS build IN2013_13.1.0.593(EX01)

Reproducing the crash reported in this PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/125533

On Android the function that pushes chunks onto the microphone input_buffer doesn't have a lock, so the lock applied when retrieving data from the input_buffer has no effect.

The problem only comes about when the threads clash and the Copy-on-write features on the `Vector<int> input_buffer` object cause the reading thread to access an invalid pointer.

This doesn't happen very often at the normal rate of fetching 20ms chunks from the input buffer `AudioServer.get_input_frames(882)` (corresponding to 44.1kHz audio). However if you get the frames one at a time then the chance of a clash is much greater and you can get the Godot app to crash in a few seconds.

This problem was found when I was using AI to explore lower latency methods on the microphone on Android deployments, but this reproduction bug is all my own work.

Basically all you need to do is the following:

```
func _ready() -> void:
	if OS.get_name() == "Android" and not OS.request_permission("android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO"):
		await get_tree().on_request_permissions_result
	AudioServer.set_input_device_active(true)

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	var read_size := 1
	while AudioServer.get_input_frames_available() >= read_size:
		var frames := AudioServer.get_input_frames(read_size)
```

Vulkan pipeline cache is discarded on next launch if the last save happened mid-compile

Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable

Android 17 - Vulkan (Mobile) - Adreno 710

On Android, the Vulkan pipeline cache is rejected on every launch, meaning shaders have to rebuild every launch. This means longer startup times. For us, this means taking 23 seconds to launch instead of 14 seconds.

The cause is that `pipeline_cache_serialize()` returns the buffer sized from an earlier size query, while the driver writes less (so the file has bytes past the header's `data_size`). The size check fails, and then it discards the cache. However, this only happens when a save is made while pipelines are still compiling.

We first noticed this because Android startup times were long compared to other platforms during testing - but were able to reproduce it on Nvidia RTX 3080 in Windows 11 as well.

Adreno 618 (Vulkan): large canvas_item shader miscompiled — screen-aligned blocks of wrong output that change every frame

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable (official Android export template, `template_release`)
- Not reproducible on desktop: same project on macOS (Metal), Forward Mobile and Forward+ render pixel-identical before/after the workaround.

Samsung Galaxy A71 (SM-A715F), Android 13 (A715FXXSBDXB1), Snapdragon 730G / **Adreno 618**, Vulkan 1.1.128 (driver reports `OpenGL ES 3.2 V@0502.0 (GIT@e1ac91e)`, 2020-11-17), renderer: Forward Mobile, `rendering/driver/threads/thread_model.android=2`.

A large `canvas_item` shader (~1300 lines, everything in one `fragment()`, used to draw building facades with lit windows) renders the lit window glass wrong on Adreno 618 only: the glass comes out dark brown (~7 % of the lamp colour) with rectangles of the correct colour on top. The rectangles are aligned to the **screen** grid, not to the geometry, and change from frame to frame, so lit windows "crawl" with blocky noise.

Before / after the workaround (crop from the device, `adb exec-out screencap`):

[image]

What we ruled out, each change tested on the device separately (noise stayed every time):

1. **Derivatives / helper invocations**: replaced every `dFdx`/`dFdy`/`fwidth` and implicit-LOD use on this path with analytic values computed from `SCREEN_MATRIX * CANVAS_MATRIX * MODEL_MATRIX`.
2. **`discard`**: replaced all three with a `break` out of a `do { } while (false)`.
3. **Early-out branches** and the overall shader size: cut whole features (doors, shop windows, one-storey buildings) out of the shader.
4. **Dynamic array indexing** of a `const` array: replaced it with a chain of selects.
5. **Precision**: forced `highp` on the inputs with large coordinates. The values involved are also small at this point.

Debug output can't show the bug. Any intermediate value printed as the colour instead of the result is smooth and correct on the device: the room light, the pane colour, the weights of glass/bars/sill, the depth values, NaN checks. Writing it out changes what the compiler produces.

The result goes wrong only when the pane colour passes through the **last statement** of a helper function:

```
vec3 window(...) {
    ...
    return mix(colour, wood, sill_band);   // sill_band is 0.0 inside the glass
}
```

Workarounds that **did not** help, all with noise still present:
- guarding with `sill_band > 0.0`;
- skipping the `mix` with a ternary (`?:`) inside the function;
- a branch whose condition includes another value computed inside the function.

The workaround that **does** help: a `bool` computed by the **caller** and passed in, with an `if` that returns before the `mix`:

```
vec3 window(..., bool in_pane) {
    ...
    if (in_pane) {
        return colour;
    }
    return mix(colour, wood, sill_band);
}
```

Side effects observed on the device:
- One diagnostic variant (one extra function call) failed pipeline creation entirely: `Couldn't create Vulkan graphics pipelines (VkResult error -13)` in logcat. Godot printed no shader error, and the layer just wasn't drawn.
- With the workaround, pipeline creation for this shader on first use got much slower (a 330–390 ms hitch became 1280–1370 ms). We now warm it up during the loading screen.

We know this is a driver/compiler bug, not a Godot bug. Filing it in case Godot keeps known-driver-issue workarounds or wants a note for Adreno 6xx. Questions:
- Is there a known Adreno 6xx SPIR-V pattern like this, for example `OpSelect` or `mix` with a uniform-false weight being miscompiled?
- Does Godot already apply any Adreno-specific workarounds in the SPIR-V path that could cover it?

Not reduced to a minimal project yet: the bug depends on the shape of the code, and small extracts so far rendered fine. The full shader and the before/after versions are available on request. If a minimal reproduction project is needed, we can keep cutting the shader down on the device until it still fails.

Not yet; see above.

A `CompositorEffect` (callback type `EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_PRE_OPAQUE`) keeps an RD texture the size of the frame and exposes it through a `Texture2DRD`, which a spatial shader samples, either as a global uniform or as a material uniform. When the size changes, the effect creates a new RD texture inside `_render_callback()` and assigns it to `Texture2DRD.texture_rd_rid`.

In that frame, every draw of the material that samples the texture fails with this error, one per draw:

```
ERROR: Uniforms supplied for set (3):
Set: 3 Binding: 0 Type: UniformBuffer Writable: N Length: 272
Set: 3 Binding: 1 Type: Texture Writable: N Length: 1
Set: 3 Binding: 2 Type: Texture Writable: N Length: 1
Set: 3 Binding: 3 Type: Texture Writable: N Length: 1
are not the same format as required by the pipeline shader. Pipeline shader requires the following bindings:
[...]
Set: 3 Binding: 0 Type: UniformBuffer Writable: N Length: 16
Set: 3 Binding: 1 Type: Texture Writable: N Length: 1
   at: draw_list_draw (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:6037)
```

The set that is supplied (a 272-byte UBO and 3 textures) belongs to the other material in the scene (`other.gdshader`). The pipeline expects the reading material's own set 3 (a 16-byte UBO and 1 texture). It looks like the reading material's uniform set is invalidated by the texture change in the middle of the frame, and the forward renderer then leaves the previously bound material set in place instead of rebuilding the set or skipping the draw. It happens to a light that sits in a shadow atlas quadrant other than the one it would like to be in, when the quadrant it would like has no free slot. The cause is in `LightStorage::shadow_atlas_update_light()` (`servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/light_storage.cpp`):

```
should_realloc = shadow_atlas->quadrants[old_quadrant].subdivision != (uint32_t)best_subdiv && (tick - ...alloc_tick > shadow_atlas_realloc_tolerance_msec);
should_redraw = shadow_atlas->quadrants[old_quadrant].shadows[old_shadow].version != p_light_version;

	shadow_atlas->quadrants[old_quadrant].shadows.write[old_shadow].version = p_light_version;
	//already existing, see if it should redraw or it's just OK
	return should_redraw;
}
...
if (found_shadow) {
[... 7 more lines]
```

When the light should move (`should_realloc`) but no slot is found (`found_shadow == false`), the function returns `should_redraw` without writing `p_light_version` into the slot the light keeps. Once the light's version has changed a single time, `version != p_light_version` is true on every later call, so the light is redrawn every frame although its version no longer changes.

| | draw calls a frame | primitives a frame |
| :-- | --: | --: |
| default quadrants, before anything moved | 65 | 822 |
| default quadrants, 3 s after one box moved 1 cm, once | 256 | 3,114 |
| default quadrants, 10 s after | 256 | 3,114 |
| all quadrants subdivided 4, before / 3 s after / 10 s after | 65 / 65 / 65 | 822 / 822 / 822 |

In the game where I ran into it (4 omni and 2 spot lights with shadows in one room), a view in which nothing moves drew 106 draw calls instead of 52 and about 127,000 primitives more, every frame.

Workaround: give all four quadrants the same subdivision, so that no light wants to be in another quadrant.

Possible fix, which I have **not** built or tested: write the version into the slot that is kept before the last return.

```
	if (old_quadrant != SHADOW_INVALID) {
		shadow_atlas->quadrants[old_quadrant].shadows.write[old_shadow].version = p_light_version;
	}

	return should_redraw;

Adjoining sin/cos calls on Apple platforms can produce different results depending on build, resulting in mesh noise

current master

MacOS 26

I was noticing when resaving meshes was creating significant diff noise. On macOS, optimized builds (template_release or -O3/-Os) can return different results from unoptimized builds (dev_build, -O0) for the same input.

Apple clang defaults to -fno-math-errno. With errno off, LLVM merges adjacent sinf(x) and cosf(x) calls into one call to Apple's __sincosf_stret. At -O0 the two calls stay separate. For some inputs, __sincosf_stret returns a cosine that is 1 ULP off from cosf.

This in particular is a problem for when we decompress vertices, tangents, and normals on meshes in the rendering server, as it calls Basis(axis, angle) -> (Basis::set_axis_angle), which has two adjoining sin and cos calls.
I hit this with Basis::set_axis_angle: at rot_angle = 2.11265922 (0x400735cf):

    cosf returns 0xbf040712.
    __sincosf_stret returns 0xbf040713.

The 1 ULP difference then shows up in the resulting basis. Debug and release builds, or different platforms, can then disagree. That is a reproducibility problem; this would be especially bad for any team modifying meshes on differing platforms.

The solution I've found is to use -fmath_errno, as this prevents __sincosf_stret optimization entirely.

1. `axis = (0.582395375, -0.566010714, -0.583478808)` (`(0x3f1517dd, 0xbf10e614, 0xbf155ede)`).
2. `angle = 0.836240172` (`0x3f5613d6`).
3. The `Basis::set_axis_angle()` then computes `rot_angle = |angle * 2 - 1| * PI = 2.11265922` (`0x400735cf`). This is the value passed to `cos` and `sin`:

| | dev (`-O0`) | release (`-O3`) |
|---|---|---|
| `cos(rot_angle)` | `0xbf040712` (-0.515732884) | `0xbf040713` (-0.515732944) |
| `sin(rot_angle)` | `0x3f5b53ee` | `0x3f5b53ee` |
| `rows[0]` | `bad45500, 3980e800, bf7fffea` | `bad45600, 3980e400, bf7fffea` |
| `rows[1]` | `bf7fe224 bcf6e8f0 3ad34700` | `bf7fe224 bcf6e8f0 3ad34700 |
| `rows[2]` | `bcf6e810, 3f7fe23a, 399a7800` | `bcf6e830, 3f7fe23a, 399a7400` |

Deadlock when using `physics/*d/run_on_separate_thread`

- Reproducible in: 960f4db5be16e2f1f7b46f9db7c824c2e0af1035 (4.8-beta)
- Reproducible in: c7a07610e956c53a5bc226e4fd6d30b1ec565166 (4.5-beta7)
- Not reproducible in: b947e5f8cc9ba7bb4e871dc3d71a850d20cbb97b (4.5-beta7)

Godot v4.8.beta (960f4db5b) - Fedora Linux 44 (Forty Four) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Single-window, 2 monitors (3840x2160 @ 239.98 Hz, 3840x2160 @ 164.82 Hz) - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (RADV GFX1201) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 60.39 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

(Found as part of reviewing #117300.)

#109591 and #117268 changed so that the physics command queue is no longer flushed during physics processing when using the `physics/*d/run_on_separate_thread` project setting, to prevent race conditions with physics queries (and some other things).

This however technically introduced a regression with the following setup:

```
extends Node3D

var done := false
@onready var body := $Body

func _thread_func() -> void:
	# This will block until its command is flushed from the queue, since it needs a return value.
	PhysicsServer3D.body_get_state(body, PhysicsServer3D.BODY_STATE_SLEEPING)

func _physics_process(_delta: float) -> void:
[... 6 more lines]
```

Prior to #109591 you could safely assume that the command queue would be flushed by the physics thread at some point, but after #109591 that responsibility essentially falls on the main thread, during physics processing specifically, and if the main thread performs synchronization with another thread that's waiting for such a flush (like in the `wait_to_finish` case above) then that obviously never happens, causing a deadlock.

Note that this is no different from how it's always behaved when `physics/*d/run_on_separate_thread` is *disabled*, but it is technically a regression to the *enabled* case none the less, so I figured I should make it known.

I don't know that there's really any good solution to this which doesn't involve significant refactoring of the approach to multi-threaded physics in general. I would also consider this a fairly niche use-case. Nobody else seems to have reported this in the year or so that this change has been live anyway.

1. Open the MRP.
2. Run the main scene.
3. Note how nothing renders, and "Successfully joined thread!" isn't printed to the Output log.

`DisplayServerWindows::_set_mouse_mode_impl()` calls `ClipCursor(nullptr)` whenever the mouse mode is not captured or confined. `_process_activate_event()` calls it on every `WA_ACTIVE` / `WA_CLICKACTIVE`. As a result, every time a Godot window is activated it clears the cursor clip rectangle, even if Godot never set a clip rectangle itself.

The cursor clip belongs to the window station, not to a desktop or window. Godot therefore also clears a clip that another application owns. Our case: automated GPU tests run Godot windows on a separate, never-switched-to Win32 desktop (`CreateDesktop` in `WinSta0`) so that they don't disturb the user. While those tests run, a fullscreen game on the user's desktop loses its cursor confinement every few seconds. The game stays in the foreground, but the mouse can leave it onto the second monitor.

Expected: Godot only releases a cursor clip that Godot itself set, for example by remembering whether its last `ClipCursor` call confined the cursor. A window in `MOUSE_MODE_VISIBLE` should leave the global clip untouched.

Relevant code (4.7.2, `platform/windows/display_server_windows.cpp`):
- `_set_mouse_mode_impl()`, else branch: `ClipCursor(nullptr);`
- `_process_activate_event()`: `_set_mouse_mode_impl(mouse_mode);` on activation

2. Start any Godot project in a normal window (`MOUSE_MODE_VISIBLE`) on a separate desktop (`CreateDesktop` plus `STARTUPINFO.lpDesktop = "WinSta0\\<name>"`), so the user's foreground window does not change.
3. As soon as the Godot window activates, `GetClipCursor()` returns the full virtual screen again: the helper's clip is gone.

Remaining reentrancy use-after-free issues in Dictionary and Array

- Reproducible on master

Linux

I reported a reentrancy issue at https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123531#discussion_r4370334936 and a fix was merged in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/124900.

But it turns out there are more of such issues. One more introduced by the optimization, but two more which are pre-existing. With this report I only mean to bring them to attention, especially since the previous one was considered important to fix. I would however also understand that this kind of API usage can't be expected to be handled correctly.

Note that the issues were found with the help of AI. They don't represent bugs experienced with Godot, though they are reproducible with the given GDScript snippets.

This is another #123531 regression. The `operator[](*key) = *value` assignment destroys the old destination value before copying, while the source value is held only by pointer reference. But the source value can be invalidated from GDScript as part of a `NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE` handler:

```
extends SceneTree

class Predeleter extends RefCounted:
	var src = null # source dict to clear during predelete
	func _notification(what):
		if what == NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE and src != null:
			src.clear() # frees the node holding the borrowed source value
			src = null
			var junk := []
			for i in 2048:
[... 15 more lines]
```

Old code copied first (`Variant value = E.value;` then `operator[](key) = value;`), so the clear could not free the owned local.

Related to the above, the same API call is reentrant on conversion with a typed Dictionary. The key is validated first, and for a matching key type it is **borrowed** (`key = &E.key`). The value is validated next and when it needs conversion, it might call into GDScript. That might trigger code that invalidates the reference to the key.

```
extends SceneTree

class RidClearer extends RefCounted:
	var src = null
	func get_rid() -> RID:
		if src != null:
			src.clear() # frees the node holding the borrowed key E.key
			src = null
			var junk := []
			for i in 2048:
[... 12 more lines]
```

In the old code, `merge()` copied the key into an owned local (`Variant key = E.key;`) and was safe.

This is pre-existing, unrelated to above mentioned PRs, except it's basically the same issue as fixed in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/124900 since it's also caused by retaining a borrowed pointer (`const Variant *source = p_array._p->array.ptr();`) which can be invalidated from GDScript.

```
extends SceneTree

class RidClearer extends RefCounted:
	var target = null # the source Array to clear mid-conversion
	func get_rid() -> RID:
		if target != null:
			target.clear() # frees the buffer Array::assign still reads
			target = null
		var junk := []
		for i in 2048:
[... 14 more lines]
```

This one is easy and cheap to fix by pinning the source as done for `append_array` in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/124900.

This one is also pre-existing. The function iterates the source map directly in `for (const KeyValue &E : p_dictionary._p->variant_map)`, but the `Variant::construct` calls within the loop can call back into GDScript, which can then modify the source map.

```
extends SceneTree

class RidClearer extends RefCounted:
	var src = null
	func get_rid() -> RID:
		if src != null:
			src.clear() # frees HashMap nodes while assign still iterates them
			src = null
			var junk := []
			for i in 2048:
[... 14 more lines]
```

Fixing this would involve copying all values before calling `Variant::construct`, which is one extra copy per converted element (but it'd be a shallow copy on the already-slow path).

Scripts to reproduce each case are already provided above.

I don't have any related Godot project.

As a skeleton gets smaller / shorter in length the accuracy of the JacobianIK3D solver becomes increasingly worse.
This issue is unaffected by the Min Distance setting in the inspector.

(Following video showcases my issue, Jacobian settings included in screenshot after video. both are taken from the included reproduction project)
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e8456fe-d7d3-48d1-9c19-8b5f25927b4d

(Max iterations and Angular delta limit just set to arbitrary highs. changing this does not affect the outcome)
[image]

**Warning: I see the problem in my scene and know it is caused by a bug in JacobianIK3D. However, I would not know what caused it. The following is my explanation of what my AI agent recognizes as the cause, and what could be a potential fix. Take this with a grain of salt**

In scene/3d/jacobian_ik_3d.cpp (line 54), JacobianIK3D::_solve_iteration tries to prevent a divide by zero with:
```
Vector3 axis = head_to_effector.cross(effector_to_destination);
if (Math::is_zero_approx(axis.length_squared())) {
    continue;
}
```
Math::is_zero_approx(double) checks against CMP_EPSILON (10^-5). This is intended for linear comparisons. Because axis.length_squared() is a squared instead of linear it needs to use CMP_EPSILON2 (10^-10). CMP_EPSILON2 is intended for use in squared comparisons.

For example: for a bone chain with a length of 0.12m (the included example scene) the solver skips joint rotation whenever the target error is below ~0.026m (idk why but it seems to be true, making the total bone chain length even smaller / lower increases the deadzone further)

**Proposed fix**
```
- if (Math::is_zero_approx(axis.length_squared())) {
+ if (axis.length_squared() < CMP_EPSILON2) {
      continue;
  }
```

Separate thread model: render thread hangs in `MaterialStorage::_update_queued_materials()` because `material_free()` unlinks from `material_update_list` without its mutex

- Reproducible in: 4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb], 4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf], 4.8.beta2.official [cafc17a19]
- Only with the Separate thread model (`rendering/driver/threads/thread_model` = Separate, or `--render-thread separate`). Not reproducible with the default (Safe) thread model.

Windows 11 (build 26200) - Godot v4.8.beta2.official [cafc17a19] - Vulkan 1.4.341 - Forward+ - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 (nvidia, 610.88) - Intel Core Ultra 5 225F (10 threads)

With the Separate thread model, the game freezes. The render thread prints these two errors alternately, forever:

```
ERROR: Condition "p_elem->_root != this" is true.
   at: remove (./core/templates/self_list.h:80)
ERROR: Condition "p_elem->_root" is true.
   at: add (./core/templates/self_list.h:46)
```

The main thread waits in `RenderingServerDefault::sync()`.

Stacks from the frozen 4.8-beta2 process (official build, symbolized with the official `.debugsymbols`):

```
Render thread ("WorkerThread 0"):
  _err_print_error
  RendererRD::MaterialStorage::_update_queued_materials()+0x282
  RendererRD::Utilities::update_dirty_resources()+0x1e
  RendererSceneCull::free(RID)+0x1ae
  CommandQueueMT::_flush()+0x97
  RenderingServerDefault::_thread_loop()+0x54
  WorkerThreadPool::_process_task(...)

Main thread:
[... 3 more lines]
```

It loops in the first loop of `_update_queued_materials()`, the one that holds `material_update_list_mutex`:

```
while (SelfList<Material> *E = material_update_list.first()) {
	material_update_list.remove(E); // fails: E->_root != &material_update_list
	copy.add(E);                    // fails: E->_root != nullptr
}
```

In the frozen process, `material_update_list.first()` is an element whose `_root` is `&copy`, the local list of that same call (read with WinDbg). So the element was already moved to `copy` earlier in the same drain, and a stale `_next` in `material_update_list` leads back to it. The doubly linked list is inconsistent.

As far as I can tell, the only change to `material_update_list` made without `material_update_list_mutex` is in `MaterialStorage::material_free()`. `material_owner.free(p_rid)` destroys the `Material`, and `~SelfList()` unlinks `update_element` without the mutex. Other threads add to the same list while holding the mutex. With RD, `can_create_resources_async()` is true, so `material_create_from_shader()` runs `material_set_shader()` → `_material_queue_update()` on the calling thread (the main thread or a loader thread) while the render thread is freeing materials. A material that is freed before the next drain (created or changed since then) is still linked when it is destroyed.

This change fixes it in my tests:

```
--- a/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/material_storage.cpp
+++ b/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/material_storage.cpp
@@ void MaterialStorage::material_free(RID p_rid) {
 	material_set_shader(p_rid, RID()); //clean up shader
 	material->dependency.deleted_notify(p_rid);
 
+	{
+		MutexLock lock(material_update_list_mutex);
+		material->update_element.remove_from_list();
+	}
[... 3 more lines]
```

The same code is still in `master`.

Enum names are constantly being reformatted for every single field

This issue exists as of this commit: c51ff06e8836a70ea905701c081bf94124dcd6ce

not system-dependent

[gdscript_compiler.cpp line 2894](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c51ff06e8836a70ea905701c081bf94124dcd6ce/modules/gdscript/gdscript_compiler.cpp#L2894) iterates over enum values and reformats them for every gdscript field that it meets.

while this is fine for small projects, it scales up rapidly as you get more fields and enum values. in my project:
  - I have an enum with 4,821 entries.
  - 930 fields use that enum.
  - Godot reformatted the same names and values separately for every field: approximately 4.48 million entries.

I measured this and found out 50.9 seconds are spent formatting enum descriptions, versus 0.26 seconds generating bytecode.

---
The fix for this is very simple and I can send a PR for it:
we can have a `HashMap<StringName, String> enum_hints;` in [GDScriptCompiler](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/gdscript/gdscript_compiler.h), which caches these. and then we simply do: `prop_info.hint_string = get_cached_enum_hint(variable_type);`
The memory usage for this cache is not that huge, however the performance change is really noticeable: `51.49 -> 0.50 seconds.` for my project.

  - generate a big enum, with thousands of enum members
  - generate many gdscript classes with fields that have that enum types.
  - observe that parsing those scripts will take massive amount of time.

(yes my classes and enums were auto-generated by protobuf, however that doesn't really change the fact that this code path is really doing heavy work)

Metal: subpass inputs are plain texture reads, so Mobile renderer subpasses never stay in tile memory

`master` (b47a795aa5), by code reading. Also 4.7.2-stable.

macOS 15, Apple M2, Metal, Mobile renderer.

[`rendering_shader_container_metal.cpp#L400`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/b47a795aa585d7bdb589f465e6ffcf15ebb31b9b/drivers/metal/rendering_shader_container_metal.cpp#L400) hard-codes `msl_options.use_framebuffer_fetch_subpasses = false`, so `subpassLoad()` (e.g. the tonemap subpass, [`tonemap_mobile.glsl#L734`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/b47a795aa585d7bdb589f465e6ffcf15ebb31b9b/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/effects/tonemap_mobile.glsl#L734)) compiles to a texture read. The driver matches that:

- input attachments are bound as ordinary textures;
- each subpass gets its own render encoder ([`render_next_subpass()`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/b47a795aa585d7bdb589f465e6ffcf15ebb31b9b/drivers/metal/metal3_objects.cpp#L1287-L1299));
- attachments used by a later subpass are stored, then loaded again ([`getMTLStoreAction()`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/b47a795aa585d7bdb589f465e6ffcf15ebb31b9b/drivers/metal/metal_objects_shared.cpp#L390-L396)).

So on Apple GPUs, which are tile-based and support framebuffer fetch, the Mobile renderer's subpasses cost the same as separate render passes: a full-screen store and load at each subpass boundary.

Is this intentional (e.g. multiview, MSAA, Intel/AMD Macs), or just not implemented yet? Not proposing a fix; enabling the flag alone wouldn't work without keeping subpasses in one encoder.

Code inspection, no visible bug. A Metal frame capture of the Mobile renderer's subpass path should show one encoder per subpass.

RenderingDevice transfer worker staging buffers never shrink, keeping ~512 MiB of host-visible memory resident after loading large textures

- Reproducible in 4.7.2-stable (ed1daf0bf).
- The relevant code is unchanged in `master` as of 2026-11-05.

Windows 11, Vulkan 1.4 (Forward+), NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti, 24 logical cores.

Creating textures **with initial data** (`texture_create` with data, which is what `ResourceLoader` does for `.ctex`, as well as `ImageTexture` / `Texture2DArray` creation) goes through `RenderingDevice`'s transfer workers. Each worker's staging buffer:

- is sized to the next power of two of the largest single upload it has seen,
- only ever grows, and
- is released only in `_free_transfer_workers()` at shutdown.

When a worker is acquired, an idle worker that is too small is preferred and grown in place over a submitted-but-not-waited worker that is already large enough. So a burst of big uploads, for example several 8192×8192 BC3/BC7 textures with full mip chains (about 85 MiB each), grows several workers to 128 MiB each.

The staging buffers are CPU/host-visible allocations made through VMA. Because `preferredLargeHeapBlockSize` is not set, they live in 256 MiB host-visible blocks, and a block stays committed as long as any allocation in it is alive.

Observed in a project that streams large atlas pages at startup:
- Two (sometimes three) 256 MiB write-combined host-visible blocks appear 5–9 s after start and stay resident until exit.
- That is about 600–650 MiB of the process working set, with nothing uploading after loading finishes.
- Inside the blocks are the transfer workers' staging buffers (128 MiB each) plus the regular staging ring.
- Lowering `rendering/rendering_device/staging_buffer/max_size_mb` does not affect these blocks. That setting only caps the regular staging ring, which is used by `texture_update` / `buffer_update`.
- Limiting the worker thread pool does not remove them either.

Workaround on the project side: create large textures without initial data and fill them with `texture_update` in chunks of 16 MiB or less. That path uses the capped staging ring, so the workers never grow.

Suggested fix (any of these):
1. Trim idle transfer workers: after N frames without use, and with no pending submission, free the staging buffer and recreate it on demand.
2. Allocate staging buffers above some threshold (e.g. 16 MiB) as dedicated VMA allocations, so freeing them actually returns memory to the OS.
3. Split large initial-data uploads into bounded chunks, so worker staging stays small.

1. Open the attached MRP and run it.
2. Eight worker-pool tasks each create a 4096×4096 RGBA8 image with mipmaps (~85 MiB) and call `ImageTexture.create_from_image()`; then the scene idles.
3. Inspect the process with VMMap (or Process Explorer → private bytes / working set). After `LOADED` is printed, write-combined private memory stays about 512 MiB higher than in a control run (`SIZE := 256` in `main.gd`) for the rest of the session, although nothing is uploading anymore.

Measured with the official 4.7.2-stable mono build (Windows 11, RTX 4070 Ti, Vulkan Forward+), resident write-combined private memory about 23 s and 38 s after start (same at both times):

| `main.gd` | write-combined resident | process working set | private bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `SIZE := 256`, `COUNT := 4` (control) | 78 MiB | 831 MiB | 1,060 MiB |
| `SIZE := 4096`, `COUNT := 4` | 334 MiB | 916 MiB | 1,649 MiB |
| `SIZE := 4096`, `COUNT := 8` (as attached) | 590 MiB | 1,175 MiB | 2,421 MiB |

The extra memory grows in 256 MiB steps with the number of large uploads and does not go away while idle.

`get_global_transform_interpolated()` can return stale cached xforms

- Reproducible in 4.8 beta 2, 3.7 dev 1, 3.6.3

All

When using 3D physics interpolation, `get_global_transform_interpolated()` relies on returning cached xforms that were calculated during a pass through the scene tree immediately prior to `_process()`.

Modifying an interpolated node xform during `_process()` is not supported in general (just for teleporting initial positions), however, non-interpolated branches are expected to move nodes during `_process()`. This means that results from `get_global_transform_interpolated()` can be stale values that were only correct _prior_ to `_process()`.

_Note that these moved chains do eventually get updated prior to rendering, in a second pass through `SceneTreeFTI` after `_process()` and prior to frame drawing. However their cached interpolated xforms are not updated during `_process()`. They aren't updated on the fly as this is less efficient compared to deferring to after `_process()`._

First reported in #125163.

Move a non-interpolated node during `_process()` when using FTI, then call `get_global_transform_interpolated()`.

Project for 3.x. It should hit an assert when run, noting that the `get_global_transform_interpolated()` value does not match one calculated manually on the fly.

[FTI_noninterpolated_inheritance.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34420867/FTI_noninterpolated_inheritance.zip)

@TokageItLab reported this recently with a simple possible fix in #125163.

It will be good to spend some time on this as although the above fix works it will have some performance implications. It's possible we can use some cache invalidation logic here to reduce the cost.

UPDATE: Fix now available in #125256 and #125258. Thanks to reusing some existing flags, these fixes are essentially free (unless one of the nodes _has_ been moved in _process()_, in which case it recalculates the stale part of the chain).

Web export with PWA, Threads Support, and "Ensure Cross Origin Isolation Headers" all enabled shows black screen on first load

- Reproducible in Godot 4.7.2 stable

- I'm not 100% sure, but the bug seems to be _only_ in the web export template JS, in a script tag in [`full-size.html`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/misc/dist/html/full-size.html#L163-L197) (see sections below for more details). On `master` neither that file nor `service-worker.js` have changed since Jan 2025, so **I _think_ this bug should reproduce on latest dev and on versions going back to at least 4.4**.

Godot v4.7.2.stable (ed1daf0bf) on Linux/Wayland (Ubuntu 26.04)

I was recently working on a GDExtension that can compile to WASM, but needs thread support. I made a test build to show a friend and wanted to host it on GitHub Pages, but it doesn't serve sites with the correct cross-origin isolation headers.

I read that the PWA "Ensure Cross Origin Isolation Headers" option can get around that limitation, so I tried it out. It works, but there's a weird issue... the first time you load the page, it only shows a black screen with the following printed to the browser console:

```
Error while registering service worker: Error: Service worker already exists.
    at mygame/:182:29
(anonymous) @ mygame/:194
Promise.catch
(anonymous) @ mygame/:193
(anonymous) @ mygame/:217
```

When I refresh the page after that, everything works fine, and every subsequent load also works fine, until I uninstall the service worker from the browser devtools or do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R, or Ctrl+Click the browser reload button).

I think this is a pretty confusing experience to ship to players! It seems this bug has been present in Godot for a while, but from testing different export flags it seems like **it requires a specific combination of export options (PWA+Threads+Ensure Headers), _and_ the server the files are hosted on has to not serve the cross-origin isolation headers itself**. So maybe most people doing web exports haven't encountered it. That said, it reproduces even on projects that don't have a native extension... an empty project with these settings also repros.

1. Create a new, empty Godot project. Save a scene (2D or 3D) and set it as the project's main scene.
2. Go to Project > Export... > Add... > Web to add a web export target.
3. In the export options, under Variant enable "Thread Support", and under Progressive Web App turn on "Enabled" and "Ensure Cross Origin Isolation Headers".
4. Click Export Project..., I think both Debug and Release show the issue but for the minimal repro I chose Release.
5. Navigate to the export folder, and in a terminal run `python -m http.server 3000` (or any other simple static server process that doesn't add extra headers by default).
6. Open a browser (I tested both Firefox and Chrome) in Incognito/Private Browsing. Navigate to `http://localhost:3000`.
7. The game will fail to load with no visible error, only a black screen.

[Godot-PWA-Minimal-Repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34258087/Godot-PWA-Minimal-Repro.zip)

This is a completely empty project, with a single 2D scene with one text label. The repro project has four different web export targets to show the issue:

1. Web, PWA enabled only: game runs on first load, no problem.
2. Web, PWA and Ensure Cross Origin Isolation Headers enabled: no problem. (Looks like "Ensure Cross Origin Isolation Headers" doesn't actually ensure headers are present [unless it detects they're needed](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/95c0fa5fe8a019adc29d074c16b64469b04571f7/misc/dist/html/full-size.html#L163-L168). Not a big deal but maybe it could be renamed or better documented at some point...)
3. Web, PWA and Thread Support enabled: game fails to load with an onscreen error about missing headers. This is expected.
4. **Web, PWA, Thread Support and Ensure Cross Origin Isolation Headers all enabled: the bug!!** Black screen on first load, ok on reloads.

When testing, remember that the service worker messes with game loading (on a re-export it'll even serve a stale version of the game, unless you uninstall the service worker from browser devtools or do a hard refresh). And just to reiterate, if the web server hosting the files serves the with the required headers, the bug never triggers either. So I think it's specifically some weird race condition or logic error in the template itself.

`Geometry3D.segment_intersects_triangle` misses short segments that clearly cross a small triangle

Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable. The code on master is the same.

`Geometry3D.segment_intersects_triangle` returns `null` for a segment that goes straight through a triangle, if the segment is short and the triangle is small.

In `core/math/geometry_3d.h` it computes `a = e1.dot(rel.cross(e2))` and returns false if `a` is near zero. That value isn't normalized. It gets smaller with segment length and triangle size. A 0.01 m segment through a 0.02 m triangle gives about 4e-6, which is under the 1e-5 limit, so it's treated as parallel. It isn't parallel.

I hit this in a game's collision tests. They checked 1 cm steps against model triangles and passed objects that had really gone through the model.

In a test of 4000 random short segments, 666 crossed a triangle. This function missed 556 of them. The same cases scaled up 1000x are all found.

```
var a := Vector3(0, 0, 0)
var b := Vector3(0.02, 0, 0)
var c := Vector3(0, 0, 0.02)
var mid := (a + b + c) / 3.0
var from := mid + Vector3.UP * 0.005
var to := mid - Vector3.UP * 0.005
print(Geometry3D.segment_intersects_triangle(from, to, a, b, c))
# prints <null>. It should be the point `mid`.
# Multiply all five points by 1000 and it returns the point.
```

Expected: the point where the segment crosses the triangle.
Actual: `null`.

Suggested fix: do the parallel test on a normalized value. For example, compare `a` against `rel.length() * e1.length() * e2.length()`, or skip the test and only reject when `a` is exactly zero.

I left out one thing I haven't tested: the `t > CMP_EPSILON` check further down looks like it could drop crossings at the very start of the segment, for the same reason. I'd test that before adding it.

Related but different: #121880 (wrong results near a sharp vertex).

My project chains videos together (like a playlist) and has a separate AudioStreamPlayer playing music (so that the music seamlessly plays over all of the videos).

When switching video streams, there's a brief, but noticeable pause in the music audio stream.

The steps are as follows:

- A `VideoStreamPlayer` plays video streams sequentially, like a playlist.
- A separate `AudioStreamPlayer` plays continuous music.
- Assigning the next video stream can cause an audible interruption. It sounds like a brief skip, click, or pop in that separate audio.
- At least on my Mac, it came across as a predictable pulse. On the Windows box I tested, it was present, but far more intermittent.

With further inspection, it was discovered that the video doesn’t need to be playing. Repeatedly assigning a cached Theora stream to a stopped player reproduces it.

The attached is a small project that I used in my own investigation. This project was AI assisted to help capture the telemetry to try to narrow the area of focus.

—

From my own findings and analysis, it seems that changing a video stream (even cached) puts a lock on a global audio output context while that stream loads and playback initializes. The process to do that is typically long enough to disrupt all audio in that global output.

[image]

Details

If `get_tree().quit()` is called while a GDScript lambda passed to `WorkerThreadPool.add_task()` is still running, and that lambda uses self (e.g. calls an instance method), the engine crashes on shutdown.

- Windows: exit code 0xC0000005, no error output.

- The crash happens after the window closes, so it looks like a normal exit in the editor. Only the exit code shows it.

4.8.beta2 fixed lambdas without self (probably #122533). A static method passed with `bind()` does not crash.

Workaround: `WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion()` before `quit()` or in `_exit_tree()`.

- Reproducible in 4.7.1.stable.mono.official

MacOS 26.7.1

A Control with an anchors preset whose grow direction was changed back to GROW_DIRECTION_END doesn't keep it across a save/load. PackedScene.pack() omits grow_vertical = 1 because it equals the class default (GROW_DIRECTION_END). When the scene is loaded, anchors_preset is applied and _set_anchors_layout_preset() calls set_grow_direction_preset(), which sets the preset's own grow direction (BOTH for Center Right). Nothing restores END, so the saved scene doesn't load as it was saved.

This also makes editor runs and exports differ. A .tscn that does contain grow_vertical = 1 loads correctly from text, but the export's text-to-binary conversion instantiates and repacks it (editor_export_platform.cpp), drops the line, and the exported game lays the control out differently. I hit it with a menu anchored Center Right that should grow only downward: correct in the editor, shifted up in the export.

Related but different: #124695 (the same conversion injects anchors_preset = 0 on instanced scene roots).

Workaround: anchors_preset = -1 (Custom). The anchors are kept as stored, and the default grow direction applies.

Android: all input stops after ~600 mouse clicks – InputEventRunnable pool leaks on ACTION_BUTTON_PRESS / ACTION_BUTTON_RELEASE

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable (official export templates, both the prebuilt APK template and the Gradle build template)

Device: Xiaomi Redmi Pad 2 Pro (model 25099RP13G), Android 16 (HyperOS), arm64-v8a - Input: USB/Bluetooth mouse + hardware keyboard - Renderer: Compatibility - Host: Linux, Godot 4.7.2.stable editor

After roughly 600 mouse clicks since app start, the app stops receiving **any** input: mouse, touch and keyboard. The game itself keeps running normally (frames render, `_process` runs, audio plays), but no input events reach the engine any more, so the app has to be killed. Logcat is flooded with:

```
W InputEventRunnable: Input event pool is at capacity
```

The number of clicks, not elapsed time, is what matters. In our logs the first warning appeared 1 ms after the 617th click (2 × 617 = 1234 ≥ 1200).

**Cause** (read from the 4.7.2 `godot-lib.template_debug.aar` with `javap`):

1. `InputEventRunnable.POOL` creates at most `MAX_POOL_SIZE = 1200` objects. Once that many exist and none is free, `obtain()` logs "Input event pool is at capacity" and returns `null`, and the caller drops the event.
2. `GodotInputHandler.handleMouseEvent(int eventAction, int buttonsMask, float x, float y, ...)` calls `InputEventRunnable.obtain()` **before** it checks the action. For actions it doesn't forward (the `default`/`4–6` branches, which include `ACTION_BUTTON_PRESS` (11) and `ACTION_BUTTON_RELEASE` (12)) it does `return false` without recycling the runnable. Every mouse click delivers one `ACTION_BUTTON_PRESS` and one `ACTION_BUTTON_RELEASE`, through `onGenericMotionEvent` → `GestureDetector` (doesn't consume) → `GodotGestureHandler.onMotionEvent` (doesn't consume unless a drag or context click is in progress) → `handleMouseEvent(MotionEvent)`. That leaks 2 runnables per click.
3. After 600 clicks (1200 / 2) every runnable is leaked and all further input is dropped.

`handleTouchEvent(MotionEvent, int, boolean)` has the same pattern: `obtain()` first, then `return false` for actions 4 and > 6 without recycling.

Both the left and the right button leak. `GodotGestureHandler` extends `SimpleOnGestureListener` but doesn't override `onContextClick`, so the context click doesn't consume the right-button events either.

**Suggested fix:** in `handleMouseEvent` and `handleTouchEvent`, check the action before calling `InputEventRunnable.obtain()`, or recycle the runnable on the early-return paths.

1. Export any project to Android (a debug export is fine).
2. Connect a mouse and left-click anywhere about 600 times (the right button behaves the same).
3. Input stops for good, and logcat shows `Input event pool is at capacity`.

To reproduce automatically with adb (no physical mouse needed), create a virtual evdev mouse with the platform `uinput` tool (`adb shell uinput -`, JSON commands: `register` a device with `EV_KEY`/`BTN_LEFT` and `EV_REL`, then `inject` `[1, 272, 1, 0, 0, 0]` / `[1, 272, 0, 0, 0, 0]` with short `delay`s). Note that `adb shell input mouse tap` does **not** reproduce it, because it only sends `ACTION_DOWN`/`ACTION_UP`, not `ACTION_BUTTON_PRESS`/`RELEASE`. With a real or `uinput` mouse, input froze between click 550 and 600 in every run (left and right button).

Use a Gradle build and drop the two actions in the activity before they reach Godot. Godot doesn't forward them to the engine anyway; the only place it uses `ACTION_BUTTON_RELEASE` is `GodotGestureHandler.onActionUp` at the end of a drag, and the following `ACTION_UP` does the same thing:

```
// GodotApp.java (Gradle build template)
private static boolean leaksInGodot(MotionEvent event) {
    int action = event.getActionMasked();
    return action == MotionEvent.ACTION_BUTTON_PRESS || action == MotionEvent.ACTION_BUTTON_RELEASE;
}

@Override
public boolean dispatchGenericMotionEvent(MotionEvent event) {
    if (leaksInGodot(event)) return false;
    return super.dispatchGenericMotionEvent(event);
[... 7 more lines]
```

With this workaround we did 1200 left clicks, 1200 right clicks and 3000 left clicks on the same device without a single "pool is at capacity" warning, and input kept working.

Any project exported to Android shows it, e.g. an empty scene with a `Label` that counts `InputEventMouseButton` presses in `_input`. The counter stops at around 600.

C#: build fails when a script class derives from a script class compiled against 4.7 (missing GodotInternal on the ancestor)

- Reproducible in: 4.8.0-dev.7, 4.8.0-beta.1 (4d10419ca).
- Not reproducible in: 4.8.0-dev.6 and earlier, 4.7.2-stable.

Godot v4.8.beta1.mono - Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 - .NET 10.0.114 (win-x64). The failure is in the C# source generator, at dotnet build; no editor or GPU involved.

A 4.8 project does not compile when a script class derives from a script class in a prebuilt assembly that was built against 4.7. The generated collector calls `Ancestor.GodotInternal.GetGodotClassTrampolines(collectors, options)`, and no 4.7-built assembly contains that nested type: the generator emits it into each script class it compiles, and it is not in `GodotSharp.dll`.

```
error CS0117: 'AncestorNode' does not contain a definition for 'GodotInternal'
```

`GetClosestBaseTypeDeclaringGodotInternalMethod` (`modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ExtensionMethods.cs:421`) returns the immediate base type unchecked: its loop continues only while `top.IsExtern`, which Roslyn's C# implementation hard-codes to `false`. `TrampolineCollectorDispatchGenerator.cs:144` then emits the call without the `IsGodotSourceGeneratorDisabled` guard that the three member calls above it use. A consumer hits this through gdUnit4's test adapter, which generates such a derived class (godot-gdunit-labs/gdUnit4Net#547). I did not build the engine from source.

**Suggested fix:** continue the loop while the type is declared outside the current compilation (`!SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(top.ContainingAssembly, classTypeSymbol.ContainingAssembly)`). It would then skip the 4.7 ancestor, reach the native base type and emit no ancestor call, which is correct — a 4.7-compiled class has no trampolines to collect.

1. Class library, `Godot.NET.Sdk/4.7.2`, `net10.0`, with `public partial class AncestorNode : Godot.Node {}`. Build it, keep `Ancestor.dll`.
2. C# project, `Godot.NET.Sdk/4.8.0-beta.1`, `net10.0`, referencing that dll, with `public partial class DerivedNode : Ancestor.AncestorNode {}`.
3. `dotnet build` in the 4.8 project.

Rebuilding `Ancestor.dll` against `4.8.0-beta.1` makes the same project compile, so the version the ancestor assembly was built against is the only variable.

`trampoline-ancestor-mrp.zip`: `Ancestor/` (4.7.2 project that produces `App/lib/Ancestor.dll`), `App/` (4.8.0-beta.1 project with the derived class), `README.md`.

```
cd Ancestor && dotnet build -o ../App/lib
cd ../App && dotnet build
```

RenderingDevice.texture_get_data_async() silently returns another texture's data when one frame's downloads approach the staging pool size

Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf]
Other versions not tested.

Godot v4.7.2.stable - SteamOS 3.9.5 (build 20261023.100), Linux 7.2.7-valve2 - Wayland (KDE) - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7700S (RADV NAVI33), Mesa 26.2.0-devel (git-5c65d4fc31), Vulkan 1.4.350 - AMD Ryzen 7 7435HS - 16 GB RAM (ASUS TUF Gaming A16 FA617NTR)

When several RenderingDevice.texture_get_data_async() downloads are queued in the same frame, and their combined size gets close to the staging pool size (rendering/rendering_device/staging_buffer/max_size_mb, default 128), one of them comes back with the wrong contents. Most or all of its data belongs to the texture downloaded just before it.

No error or warning is printed, even with --verbose. The callback fires normally, and the buffer has the correct size, so the corruption is silent.
It happens below the pool size. At 2560×1440 RGBA16F (28.1 MB per texture), four textures totalling 112.5 MB already trigger it.
It's deterministic. The same texture index is hit on every run, with the same number of wrong texels.
The GPU data is correct. The synchronous texture_get_data() returns the same textures correctly, and so does texture_get_data_async() once the downloads are spread over several frames.
A bigger pool hides it. Setting max_size_mb=256 (via override.cfg) makes the same case come back correct.
Measured with the attached MRP. Every texture is RGBA16F, cleared to its own constant colour with texture_clear(), then read back in one frame:

Textures × size	Total	Result
3 × 2560×1440 (28.1 MB)	84.4 MB	all correct
4 × 2560×1440	112.5 MB	texture 3: 3,645,440 of 3,686,400 texels wrong, holding texture 2's value
5, 6 and 7 × 2560×1440	140.6–196.9 MB	texture 3 wrong, identical counts; all others correct
7 × 2560×1440, sync texture_get_data()	196.9 MB	all correct
7 × 2560×1440, max_size_mb=256	196.9 MB	all correct
7 × 1920×1080 (15.8 MB)	110.7 MB	all correct
8 × 1920×1080	126.6 MB	texture 7: 229,376 of 2,073,600 texels wrong, holding texture 6's value
9 and 12 × 1920×1080	142.4–189.8 MB	texture 7 wrong, identical counts; all others correct
2 × 4096×2048 (64 MB)	128.0 MB	texture 1: 6,291,456 of 8,388,608 texels wrong, holding texture 0's value
What the numbers suggest (inference, not verified in the engine source):

One texture per frame: only one download per frame is affected, namely the one whose staging space reaches the end of the pool. Downloads after it come back correct.
Region-sized corruption: the wrong texels always come in whole multiples of 4,096 texels. That's one 64×64 download region (texture_download_region_size_px = 64): 3,645,440 = 890 regions, 229,376 = 56, 6,291,456 = 1,536.
Stale data: the wrong data is always the previous download's.
So my guess is that when the download staging pool fills up and its blocks are reused, the regions copied out for that download are read from blocks that still hold the previous download's data. Either the GPU-to-staging copy for those regions isn't waited on, or it's ordered wrongly against the reuse.

We hit this in a real project. A debug tool reads back about 200 MB of compute results in one frame, and one tensor came back partly overwritten by another, which our parity tests caught. Our workaround is to spread readbacks over several frames, staying well under the pool size.

Unzip the MRP and run it from a terminal (it quits by itself): godot --path staging_overflow_mrp -s mrp.gd
It defaults to 7 textures of 2560×1440.
Options: -- --count=N --size=WxH changes the case, and -- --sync uses texture_get_data() instead.
Expected: RESULT: 0 of 7 textures read back wrong.
Actual: texture 3: CORRUPT, 3645440 of 3686400 texels wrong ... sampled texel value 0x3c003a8038003200 ... (texture 2's value) and RESULT: 1 of 7 textures read back wrong.
With -- --count=3 it passes; with -- --count=4 it fails the same way.
Add override.cfg next to project.godot containing:

[rendering]
rendering_device/staging_buffer/max_size_mb=256
With it, the default case passes.
The core of the MRP. Everything runs on the main RenderingDevice via RenderingServer.call_on_render_thread:

```
func _create() -> void:  # frame A
	for i in count:
		var f := RDTextureFormat.new()
		f.format = RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R16G16B16A16_SFLOAT
		f.width = size.x
		f.height = size.y
		f.usage_bits = RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_USAGE_SAMPLING_BIT \
				| RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_USAGE_CAN_COPY_FROM_BIT | RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_USAGE_CAN_COPY_TO_BIT
		var t := rd.texture_create(f, RDTextureView.new())
		rd.texture_clear(t, Color((i + 1) / 16.0, 0.5, 1.0 - (i + 1) / 16.0, 1.0), 0, 1, 0, 1)
[... 5 more lines]
```

Each result is then compared byte for byte with an Image of the same size filled with the same colour in FORMAT_RGBAH.

staging_overflow_mrp.zip (attached): project.godot (Forward+, no settings changed) and mrp.gd.

Not established:

Whether other GPUs or drivers are affected; only RADV on an RX 7700S was tested.
Whether uploads (texture_update and similar) have an equivalent problem.
The exact threshold. It falls between 110.7 and 126.6 MB with 15.8 MB textures, and between 84.4 and 112.5 MB with 28.1 MB textures, which suggests it depends on where each download lands in the pool rather than on the total alone.

- Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable (official build), which already includes #116524

macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Apple M5, 16 GB RAM. Godot v4.7.2.stable, Forward+ (Metal). Vorssaint 3.4.2 (`com.vorssaint.utils`)

#104246 was fixed by #116524, which turns on `wake_for_events` only when Magnet (`com.crowdcafe.windowmagnet`) is running. The same problem still happens with other apps that query windows through the Accessibility API. Magnet is probably not the only app that does this.

With the Godot editor open and idle, and the utility app **Vorssaint** running:

- **Cmd+Tab** is very slow, sometimes unresponsive, while Vorssaint's *Switcher* feature (its Cmd+Tab replacement) is enabled.
- **Clicking Godot's Dock icon** lags while Vorssaint's *Click Dock icon to cycle windows* feature is enabled.

Turning off each of those features removes the matching lag. Godot is the only app affected.

What I observed:

- While switching apps, the Godot process uses only ~1–2% CPU. A `sample` of the editor shows the main thread almost entirely in `nanosleep` from the frame-delay path (`OS_Unix::add_frame_delay`). So it isn't busy, it just doesn't wake up for incoming Accessibility requests.
- Setting `interface/accessibility/accessibility_support` to Disabled does **not** help.
- Lowering `interface/editor/timers/unfocused_low_processor_mode_sleep_usec` (100000 → 6900) does **not** help.
- In #104246, users reported similar lag with AeroSpace, so the problem doesn't seem limited to one app.

**Suggestion**

Hard-coding bundle IDs won't keep up, because any window manager, app switcher or Dock enhancement that uses the Accessibility API can trigger this. Possible options:

- Wake the run loop for Accessibility events whenever any process is a trusted Accessibility client (not only screen readers or Magnet), or always on macOS when the editor is in low-processor mode.
- Or add an editor setting to force `wake_for_events`.
- At minimum, add `com.vorssaint.utils` next to Magnet in the check from #116524.

2. Open any project in the Godot editor (an empty project is enough) and leave it idle.
3. Use Cmd+Tab between Godot and other apps, or click Godot's Dock icon from another app.

NavigationRegion3D update lost when two navmesh updates land one physics frame apart (region async iterations on)

- Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf]

Windows 11 Pro (build 26200), Godot v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf], run with `--headless`. Intel Core i9-14900K, 32 GB RAM.

When a NavigationRegion3D receives two navigation mesh updates exactly **one physics frame apart**, and region async iterations are enabled (the default), the second update never reaches the navigation map. The map keeps the first update permanently (checked after 60 and 300 physics frames). Nothing else triggers a resync until the region gets another update.

- Gap of 0, 2 or 3 physics frames: the second update arrives every time.
- `region_set_use_async_iterations(rid, false)`: the second update arrives every time, at any gap.
- It happens whether the change is made by editing the same NavigationMesh in place (`emit_changed()`), by assigning a new NavigationMesh to `navigation_mesh`, or by calling `NavigationServer3D.region_set_navigation_mesh()` directly.
- `NavigationServer3D.map_force_update()` does not recover it. Pushing the same final navmesh again (a later `region_set_navigation_mesh()`) does.

Expected: the map always ends up with the latest navigation mesh of the region.

Observed in practice with runtime rebakes (e.g. building obstacles in consecutive frames): agents keep pathing through geometry that the final navmesh excludes.
